raw_case_text:
The patient was a 38-year-old, black, single female from the state of Rio de Janeiro, who was HIV positive (diagnosed in August 2014, presenting with pneumonia and herpes zoster), with irregular use of antiretroviral therapy - tenofovir 300 mg + lamivudine 300 mg + efavirenz 600 mg. At the time of admission, the HIV viral load was recorded at 2,558 copies per mL, with TCD4+ lymphocyte counts at 170 cells/mm3 and TCD8+ lymphocytes at 1,478 cells/mm3. The patient had been diagnosed as a carrier of NF1 during childhood. At the time of hospitalization, the patient had axillary ephelides (Fig. 1), cafe-au-lait spots, and neurofibromas in the frontal trunk (Fig. 2), upper limbs, and lower limbs. Her family members (mother and sister) also presented with neurofibromas.
In June 2014, she noticed a mobile, fibroelastic mass of approximately 1 cm in the right inguinal region accompanied by hyperemia, flushing, edema, and local pain of high intensity, pulsatile, without mitigating or aggravating factors. She also had nocturnal sweating, dry cough, and unmeasured and unmedicated fever. The symptoms evolved, with worsening of the pain and a progressive increase of the mass, with fistulization of liquid and whitish secretion with traces of blood. She also reported a weight loss of 13 kg in 5 months. The patient denied dyspnea, gastrointestinal tract abnormalities, inappetence, and insomnia.
At the time of admission, there were palpable posterior cervical lymph nodes, palpable left popliteal lymph nodes without phlogistic signs, and palpable liver with 20 cm hepatimetry. The hemogram showed pancytopenia, and the patient underwent a platelet transfusion. Computed tomography of the chest revealed bronchiectasis and the absence of a mediastinal mass. A biopsy of the inguinal mass was performed, and the histopathological examination revealed a peripheral CD8+ T-cell lymphoma (Fig. 3) and HTLV-1 serology, with a nonreactive result.
After diagnosis, the patient was staged as stage III according to Ann Arbor Staging. She received treatment with a CHOEP (cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, etoposide and prednisone) chemotherapy cycle during hospitalization, presenting a satisfactory evolution with a reduction of lymph node size in the posterior cervical, left popliteal, and right inguinal regions. Outpatient follow-up was conducted at the Immunology and Hematology Department to complete 5 more CHOEP cycles, clinical evaluation, and antiretroviral treatment follow-up.
In 2 years, there was no recurrence of lymphoma. We also observed a weight gain of 21 kg, undetected viral load and the CD4+ T-lymphocyte count increased to 231 copies/mm3.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 38-year-old Black female with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) and HIV infection presented with a progressively enlarging, severely painful, fistulizing right inguinal mass, fever, night sweats, dry cough, and a 13 kg weight loss over 5 months.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: In June 2014, the patient noticed a 1 cm mobile fibroelastic right inguinal mass accompanied by local erythema, edema, and intense pulsatile pain, along with unmeasured fevers, night sweats, dry cough, and a 13 kg weight loss over 5 months. The right inguinal mass progressively enlarged and fistulized, draining blood-tinged whitish fluid. She had been diagnosed with HIV in August 2014 (after presenting with pneumonia and herpes zoster) and took tenofovir/lamivudine/efavirenz irregularly.
subjective.past_medical_history: Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) diagnosed in childhood (mother and sister also affected with neurofibromas); HIV infection diagnosed in August 2014 following pneumonia and herpes zoster, with irregular adherence to tenofovir 300 mg + lamivudine 300 mg + efavirenz 600 mg.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for painful fistulizing right inguinal mass, fever, night sweats, dry cough, and 13 kg weight loss over 5 months; negative for dyspnea, gastrointestinal symptoms, anorexia, or insomnia. Home medications: tenofovir 300 mg, lamivudine 300 mg, and efavirenz 600 mg (irregular adherence).

objective.physical_examination: Cutaneous stigmata of NF1 including axillary freckling (Crowe sign), café-au-lait macules, and multiple cutaneous neurofibromas over the anterior trunk and upper and lower extremities. Lymphatic and abdominal exam revealed a large, tender, erythematous, fistulizing right inguinal mass draining blood-streaked whitish fluid, palpable non-tender posterior cervical and left popliteal lymphadenopathy, and hepatomegaly (20 cm liver span).
objective.routine_investigations: Complete blood count demonstrated pancytopenia requiring platelet transfusion. HTLV-1 serology was nonreactive.
objective.advanced_workup: Admission lymphocyte subsets showed CD4+ T-cell count 170 cells/mm3 and CD8+ T-cell count 1,478 cells/mm3. Chest CT showed bronchiectasis without a mediastinal mass. Incisional biopsy and histopathology/immunohistochemistry of the right inguinal mass confirmed peripheral CD8+ T-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma (Ann Arbor Stage III).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Ann Arbor Stage III peripheral CD8+ T-cell lymphoma arising in a 38-year-old woman with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) and HIV infection (admission plasma HIV viral load 2,558 copies/mL, CD4+ count 170 cells/mm3, CD8+ count 1,478 cells/mm3; HTLV-1 negative). Treated with 6 cycles of systemic CHOEP chemotherapy (cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, etoposide, and prednisone; cycle 1 inpatient, cycles 2–6 outpatient) alongside reinforced adherence to tenofovir/lamivudine/efavirenz. At 2-year follow-up, she remained in complete lymphoma remission with a 21 kg weight gain, undetectable HIV viral load, and CD4+ count increased to 231 cells/mm3.
